subject: general
question: In a certain code language, 'BAYONET' is written as '2176552' and 'JOKE' is written as '1625'. How will 'HAPPIER' be written as in that language?
solution:
According to the English alphabets and their positional values: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2279b560b10991887192eff3a548e57e9b0820d787d416555b032b86f014a220.png] 

The pattern followed in the given codes is:

 **Alphabets with double digits positional values are the sum of both numbers.

 Alphabets with single-digit positional values are coded as it is.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7737eb85cd773dd6541bbb830a809087cebf75d41b75509689533e90ff4450a9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e757a8bc29977e49d148b6fdb4ed8a6cee527da9c6350e35ce191523be18f481.png] 

Similarly,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e44e2f270dcdc3ef56df72aea06aadc9061a256b31c566c14c69227af4477a12.png] 

Hence **the correct answer is option 4)**
